title: Heatmap Advisor: Pool Utilization Timeline and Burst Recommendation Composer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Operators managing Dedicated GPU pools lack a compact, actionable view that links per-GPU utilization/thermal patterns with recommended burst/oversubscription profiles and one-click canary rollout controls. Current consoles show separate charts (utilization, node health, autoscale events) but no synthesized guidance; ops frequently hand-tune burst windows after incidents, increasing mean-time-to-recover and cost.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A prototype heatmap timeline shows per-node and per-GPU utilization (last 72h) with hover details and thermal overlay.
2) The UI surfaces a generated ‘Burst Recommendation’ with rationale (expected cost delta, estimated latency impact, risk score).
3) Operators can stage a canary rollout applying the burst policy to a selector (e.g., 10% of pools or named pool) with rollback and audit metadata.
4) Telemetry hooks documented: exposures for suggestion acceptance, rollout start/stop, and observed delta vs expected.
5) Design has been reviewed by Eng and PM and usability tested with two SREs, with changes tracked in updates.
proposal_summary: Deliver a compact composer card to be added to Dedicated > Pool detail. The card contains: (A) stacked heatmap (node rows × time columns) with color encoding for utilization and a thin thermal strip for GPU temps; (B) a small ‘advisor’ pane that shows 2–3 ranked burst profiles (aggressive/moderate/conservative) with predicted unit-cost and latency tradeoffs; (C) rollout controls: selector, canary percentage slider, schedule window, and quick rollback button; (D) small link to ‘explain’ modal showing the rules used to compute recommendations (prefix cache, typical sequence lengths, percentiles).
design_decisions: Use a 72-hour default window — long enough to capture diurnal patterns but small enough for fast render
Color normalization: utilization is primary color channel, temperature uses a secondary thin stripe to avoid conflation
Advisor will propose at most 3 profiles to reduce choice paralysis
Canary percentages limited to presets: 5%, 10%, 25% to reduce risk of accidental wide rollout
Make rollout actions async with clear state machine: staging -> active -> rollback -> complete
tradeoffs: Pro: Compact card reduces navigation but Con: may overload Pool detail page if we add too many controls — we mitigate with collapse state
Pro: Auto-generated recommendations speed decisions but Con: require robust telemetry and labeling to avoid operator mistrust
Showing per-GPU detail is high-fidelity but costly on mobile — we provide a simplified aggregated view for small screens
